To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of employees’ fit with their organization and job on their job satisfaction as well as on their turnover intention are moderated by perceived organizational support, while the effects of employees value fit with their supervisors on these outcomes are not significant.

value fit with the organization increases job satisfaction and organizational citizenship behavior, while having no direct impact on turnover intentions; job fit increases job satisfaction and decreases turnover intentions.

employees' fit with the organization, their jobs, and their supervisors have different effects on their attitudes and behaviours, while perceived organizational support moderates the effects of fit on job satisfaction, organizational attachment, and turnover intentions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of fit and POS on employee outcomes in the context of Turkish banks.
the importance of the simultaneous effects of fit on employees' job satisfaction, organizational citizenship behaviour and turnover intention in the Turkish banking industry.
a relatively unexplored topic in the field, namely the simultaneous effect of employees' fit on their job satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

employees' value congruence with their organization, needs–supplies fit with their job and perceived organizational support are important factors that should be considered simultaneously to understand and manage the employee outcomes in Turkish banking industry.
employees who perceive a high level of support from their organizations tend to be satisfied with their jobs and committed to the organization, and are less likely to leave their current job.

the effects of employees’ value and needs–supplies fit with their organization and job on their job satisfaction as well as the effects of employees value fit with their job and supervisor on turnover intention are suppressed when employees perceive that their organization supports them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
POS moderates the relationship between employees' fit and their job satisfaction and commitment, and the relationship between their fit with their job and turnover intention.

employees' value–organization fit is the most important predictor of their job satisfaction and turnover intentions, while employees' value fit and needs-supplies fit with their supervisor are not related to their job satisfaction and intentions to leave their job.
employees who are fit with their organization and job are more satisfied with their job and committed to their organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simultaneous effect of employees' fit on their job satisfaction is positive and that their fit with the organization and the job are positively associated with their organizational commitment.

employees' value–organization fit is a significant antecedent of job satisfaction, organizational attachment, and turnover intention, whereas job fit is an antecedent of only job satisfaction and turnover.
POS is a powerful moderator of the effects of employee fit with organizations, job and supervisors on major outcomes in Turkish banking organizations.
